messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: how to make "mirt "and CFA in "lavaan" parameters comparable
parts:
Here is a toy example on how to transform lavaan parameters into the threshold/slope parametrization from IRT


library(mirt)
library(lavaan)

dat <- ltm::Abortion
head(dat)
colnames(dat) <- paste0("Item_",1:4)


fit_mirt <- mirt(dat, 1, itemtype = "2PL")
summary(fit_mirt)
coef(fit_mirt, IRTpars=F, simplify=T) ## intercept/slope
coef(fit_mirt, IRTpars=T, simplify=T) ## threshold/slope


sem_2pm_model = '
# loadings
theta =~ l1*Item_1 + l2*Item_2 + l3*Item_3 + l4*Item_4

# thresholds
Item_1 | th1*t1
Item_2 | th2*t1
Item_3 | th3*t1
Item_4 | th4*t1

# use thresholds to get difficulty/b
diff_1 :=  th1 / l1
diff_2 :=  th2 / l2
diff_3 :=  th3 / l3
diff_4 :=  th4 / l4

# convert loadings to discrimination/a
discrm_1 := l1 / sqrt(1-l1^2)*1.702
discrm_2 := l2 / sqrt(1-l2^2)*1.702
discrm_3 := l3 / sqrt(1-l3^2)*1.702
discrm_4 := l4 / sqrt(1-l4^2)*1.702
'
sem_2pm <- cfa(sem_2pm_model, data=dat, std.lv=T)
summary(sem_2pm)
pars_sem <- parameterestimates(sem_2pm)

#### these are the equivalent parameters
subset(pars_sem, op == ":=")
coef(fit_mirt, IRTpars=T, simplify=T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: how to make "mirt "and CFA in "lavaan" parameters comparable
parts: why you apply D=1.702 in the lavaan discrimination parameters

Because his example used a 2PL (i.e., logistic, not normal-ogive / probit) IRT model, whereas lavaan uses the probit link.

https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/228629/conversion-of-irt-logit-discrimination-parameter-to-factor-loading-metric
